chunks: I passed by Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while he had lodged at al-Hira. He said to me: 'What is your occupation?' I said: 'Animal trader.' So he said: 'Find a fazaa mule for me.' I said: 'May I be sacrificed for you! And what is al-fazaa?' He said: 'Dark, with a white belly, white thighs, and a white mouth.' He said: So I said: 'By Allah! I have not seen the likes of this description.'

So I returned from his presence, and after a while I entered the ditch (market), and suddenly there was a slave who had been riding a mule of this very description. So I asked the slave: 'Whose mule is this?' He said: 'My master's.' I said: 'Will he sell it?' He said: 'I do not know.' So I followed him until I came to his master and I bought it from him, and I came to him (the Imam) with it. So he said: 'This is the description I wanted.'

I said: 'May I be sacrificed for you! Supplicate to Allah for me.' So he said: 'May Allah amplify your wealth and your children.' He said: So I became the most abundant of the people of al-Kufa in wealth and children.

key_terms.جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ: A devotional formula of respect: 'May I be sacrificed for you' — used by companions addressing the Imams
key_terms.دَهْمَاءُ: Dark/bay in color — describing the dominant dark coat of the mule
key_terms.عِلَاجُكَ: Your trade/occupation — a colloquial Classical Arabic term for one's profession or livelihood
key_terms.فَضْحَاءُ: Fazaa — a specific type of mule, dark (bay) in body but with distinctively white belly, inner legs, and lips

ai.seo_question: What story does al-Kafi contain about Imam al-Sadiq and a mule trader from al-Hira?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates how Tarkhan al-Nakhkhas, an animal trader, encountered Imam al-Sadiq (AS) at al-Hira. The Imam requested a very specifically described mule — dark-colored with white belly, white inner thighs, and white lips — a description considered rare. After miraculously finding exactly such an animal in the marketplace, the narrator brought it to the Imam who confirmed it matched. As a reward for his service, Imam al-Sadiq supplicated for his wealth and children to be increased, and the narrator reports that this blessing was fulfilled, making him among the most wealthy and blessed with children in Kufa.
